integrator_questions: With wheel_track at 0.10 m and the sensor row at 80 mm, does the controller need less kp or more kd to hold the signal stable on the s-bend and slalom?
Where does max_error occur now, at bend entry or during recovery? Compare with iteration 3 at 0.12 m track.
Does steering_oscillation rise with the narrower track, and does line_loss_events change on the slalom?

intent: Single-variable test on the best geometry so far (iteration 3). Keep the 80 mm sensor row, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.8 kg mass, 0.03 m wheels and 0.12 m body width. Change only wheel_track, from 0.12 to 0.10 m, to test whether more turn authority reduces the peak off-track excursion (max_error about 0.062 m). Expected: max_error at or below 0.06 m, progress above 0.23 on the oval, and a score above 69.
learning: Iterations 0 to 3 show a monotone lookahead trend: 40 mm gave 52.25, 60 mm gave 65.96 and 80 mm gave 69.18 (the contract maximum). Lookahead is now at its limit, so further gains must come from other geometry levers. Iteration 1 confounded mass, track, sensor size and pitch, so none of those effects are known. This iteration isolates wheel_track alone. If it helps, the next single-variable tests are mass (lower yaw inertia) and sensor pitch. If it hurts, the optimum track is near 0.12 m and the next test is mass alone.
rationale: Iteration 3 scored 69.18, the best so far. Sensor row position has a monotone effect on score: 40 mm gave 52.25, 60 mm gave 65.96, and 80 mm gave 69.18, all on the same 0.8 kg, 0.12 m track, 12 mm sensor baseline. Max error sits at 0.062 to 0.065 m on every track in all three runs, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, while RMS error stays at 0.019 to 0.033 m. The failure is therefore a transient peak at bends, not a steady offset. Lookahead is now at the contract maximum (0.08 m), so it cannot be pushed further. Iteration 1 changed mass, track, sensor size and pitch together and lost score, so those effects are still unresolved. The next single-variable test is wheel track. Narrowing it from 0.12 to 0.10 m, with mass held at 0.8 kg, raises turn rate per unit wheel difference (turn rate = (vR - vL)/track). That gives more correction authority on tight bends, where the peak error occurs. I keep the 80 mm row, 12 mm sensors and 12 mm pitch so that any score change can be attributed to track alone. Expected result: max error near or below 0.06 m, progress above 0.23 on the oval, and a score above 69. Confidence is moderate, and the risk is extra oscillation from higher effective gain.
